text.content:
The world's city nets, linked again over the Old NET's bones.

Region: Everywhere: from NetWatch's gates down to the chrome in your skull
Controlled by: NetWatch at the gates; Night Corp on the CitiNet; owners and their ICE in each architecture
The feel of it: A city again, with roads, cops, tolls, and a bad neighborhood nobody is allowed into
Notable locations: The CitiNet, private architectures, pirate nets, and the Blackwall
Danger: Quickhacking a person is assault; diving an architecture is burglary; going near the Blackwall is NetWatch's business

Before the DataKrash of 2022 the NET was one worldwide place. For twenty-five years after it there were only sealed local nets, and data went from city to city in a courier's pocket. Since the Linkup (2049–2060) every city's net is linked into one interconnected NET, with NetWatch guarding each junction. In 2070 there's a Neuroport in nearly every skull and a network chip in every car, door and vending machine.

The Layers

  • The NET: the city nets, linked over the old trunk lines. Data, calls and money cross it; runners don't. You dive a city from inside it.
  • The CitiNet: Night City's own network of public access points, calls, eddie transfers, NCART, traffic, cameras and feeds, run by Night Corp and audited by NetWatch. Calls inside the city are free; calls outside cost a fortune, because every gate takes a cut.
  • Architectures: private systems, from a corp floor to a landlord's door locks, behind whatever ICE their owners paid for.
  • Neuroports and networked things: the chrome in your head, your car, the drone overhead, the turret on the wall.
  • Pirate nets: the Voodoo Boys' net in Pacifica, mesh nets in the Combat Zones, Northside's chrome-punk feeds.
  • Beyond the Blackwall: the Old NET, the RABIDs, and whatever else lives there.

Two Trades

Quickhackers, or glitchers, run in the street from a Cybersuite in their Neuroport, out to fifty meters in the middle of a firefight. Deep divers, or bathers, go under, body cooled in an ice bath or a netrunning chair, mind going floor by floor through an architecture; the risk is Burnout, the Flicker's death. Kabuki and Little China bathhouses rent ice baths by the hour.

The Law on the Wire

Owning a deck is legal; decks from Downtown come registered to your Neuroport, and Kabuki's back-stall decks don't. Quickhacking a person is assault, and quickhacking a cop is assault on an officer. Diving an architecture without permission is burglary, though corps would rather let their Black ICE handle it. Black ICE is legal if NetWatch licensed it, and most of it is.

What Runners Believe

Nobody dives at midnight on 8 September. Don't follow an old trunk line down. There are voices in the old lines: names, pieces of conversation, a dead friend saying hello. NetWatch calls it signal noise. And the Voodoo Boys know something.

Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.06
